query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A minor compositional modification that substitutes approximately 2 at.% of a ductile transition metal (e.g., vanadium) for Ni in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 will enhance the mechanical integrity (reduce cracking) without appreciably degrading the alloy’s caloric performance.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with poor integrity (prone to cracking) and high caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field conditions.
generation.intervention: Introduce ~2 at.% vanadium substitution for Ni, i.e. modify the composition to (Mn(Ni0.98V0.02)Si)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
generation.conditions: Under similar applied magnetic fields and pressure fields as the baseline tests, with temperature and loading regimes consistent with device operation conditions (room temperature to moderate elevated temperatures, cyclic loading, and field cycling).
generation.structural_mediator: The added vanadium is expected to create local lattice distortions and refine the microstructure, promoting a more crack‐resistant matrix by impeding crack initiation and propagation through fine precipitate or solid-solution strengthening.
generation.mechanism: By altering the local bonding environment and producing a controlled degree of lattice strain, the vanadium addition increases the alloy’s resistance to mechanical degradation (e.g., cracking) while leaving the mechanisms responsible for the caloric effect (i.e. field-induced phase transitions) largely unaltered.
generation.predicted_outcome: An improvement in mechanical integrity as evidenced by an increase in compressive strength (e.g., on the order of 10–20% higher than the baseline 152–218 MPa from previous composite studies) with minimal (<5% change) loss in the caloric response metrics (e.g., adiabatic temperature change under applied fields remains similar).
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, which exhibits high caloric performance but suffers from low mechanical integrity and cracking.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold under the tested field intensities, temperature regimes and cyclic loading conditions typical for caloric and mechanical performance measurements in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
generation.uncertainty: The precise effect of a 2 at.% vanadium substitution on both mechanical strength and caloric performance requires experimental validation; there is uncertainty regarding the optimum doping level and whether the introduced lattice strains might subtly influence the caloric response.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the baseline (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 and another set with 2 at.% V substituting for Ni. Subject both sets to identical processing conditions, then test them under controlled applied magnetic fields and pressure-fields while performing standardized compressive strength tests and caloric (e.g., adiabatic temperature change) measurements.
measurements: Compressive strength (MPa) under the same loading conditions
Caloric response (e.g., adiabatic temperature change or entropy change) under defined field strengths
Microstructural analysis (e.g., SEM, TEM) to assess crack propagation and phase distribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the V-doped alloy does not increase compressive strength by at least ~10% relative to the baseline or if the caloric response decreases by more than ~5% compared to the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
